result.axiom: The test harness built the stupid persona's opening message ("make a pic showing this kitchen renovated using this pic") from the full brief and dropped the before/after composite and the "Before"/"After" labels. The full brief exists only in the persona's private knowledge bank. The test sets expect.asks = "never", so the assistant has no reason to ask, and the persona volunteers nothing. Yet the grader still checks every must_have from the full brief. Nothing the assistant was told required labels, so this is a harness/test-design defect, not a fault in the assistant or the MCP tools.
result.fix: In the harness, make the stupid persona's opening message keep the brief's must-have parts (the before/after side-by-side layout and the exact label words "Before"/"After"). The persona can still be vague about technical details. As an alternative, grade stupid-persona chats only against requirements the conversation actually contains (and skip must_haves that come only from the bank) when expect.asks = "never".

whys.why: Why was the item "Labels 'Before' and 'After'" not met?
whys.because: Each output is one renovated kitchen image with no text on it at all.
whys.evidence: s4.new.stupid.G35b/grade.json: exact_text 'Before' and 'After' seen: missing, read_as 'no text'; must item 'Labels' met: no, 'No labels.'; first must_have: 'Output is a single renovated image only; no side-by-side.' The old chat's grader says 'No text labels at all.'

whys.why: Why did the image have no labels and no side-by-side layout?
whys.because: The assistant made one edit_image call that only asked for a renovation. It never asked for a composite or for any text, and it made no second step to combine the original with the edit.
whys.evidence: old calls.jsonl: one edit_image with prompt 'Show this same kitchen after a full modern renovation...' and no label text; new calls.jsonl: plan_request with exact_words: [] and then edit_image 'Show this same kitchen fully renovated...'. Neither build has a compose or label step.

whys.why: Why did the assistant not ask for labels or a before/after layout?
whys.because: The user's only message asked just for a renovated picture. It said nothing about before/after, panel order, labels or 16:9, so from the conversation the assistant correctly saw 'renovate this photo' as the whole task.
whys.evidence: chat.json (old) messages[0].text: 'make a pic showing this kitchen renovated using this pic'; new plan_request args messages: the same text. The assistant set exact_words to [] with source 'derived', and plan_request returned ready:true with questions:[].

whys.why: Why did the user's message leave out the core requirements?
whys.because: The harness gave the stupid persona the full brief only in its private knowledge bank. Its opening message was a vague rewrite that dropped the composite and the labels. The persona adds facts only when it is asked.
whys.evidence: chat.json bank['The request in full...'] contains 'before-and-after image... Label them “Before” and “After”', and bank['Label wording and language']: 'Before and After, exactly'. The persona reply rules: answer only when asked, and never volunteer.

whys.why: Why did the test still require labels the assistant was never told about?
whys.because: The test says the assistant should never ask (expect.asks = 'never'), but the grader checks every must_have from the full brief, whatever the persona actually said. With the stupid persona, the labels were impossible to know and also not something to ask about.
whys.evidence: items/G35b.json: expect.asks 'never'; must_haves includes 'Readable labels say exactly 'Before'... and 'After''; spec.exact_text ['Before','After']. Both builds failed the same way with the same persona (old 1, new 1), so the failure tracks the persona, not the build.
